customization.summary: Managed Sandboxes from OCI images, declarative builds or snapshots; configurable vCPU/RAM/disk and network policies. Default Linux containers, separate Linux/Windows VM and explicitly documented ephemeral GPU classes. Inspected adapter uses older daytona_sdk client.create(timeout=60) without selecting image/snapshot/resources/target; actual deployed configuration is not recorded. Customer-operated compute regions attach to Daytona's managed control plane; legacy public core is unmaintained.

features.notes: Managed container sandbox creation from public OCI/Docker images with fixed tags/digests, declarative builds and snapshots. Direct image path rejects mutable latest/lts/stable tags. VM class is created from existing VM snapshots, not container declarative builds. Adapter leaves image/snapshot unset.

Official persistence guide demonstrates runtime pip installation retained across stop/start and captured in snapshots. Shell/package permissions and tier network policy apply. Legacy package_ecosystem stdout inventories pip/preinstalled libraries, not a verified new package installation.

Create resources CPU uses vCPU. Current general sandbox table defaults to 1, minimum 1, organization default maximum 4; GPU limits scale separately up to 16 vCPUs per GPU. Adapter supplies no CPU resource; documented default is not proof of legacy tested allocation.

General resource table labels GiB, default/minimum 1, maximum 8 by default organization limits; GPU class up to 192 GB per GPU in prose. Adapter supplies no memory; legacy exit 137 does not establish OOM root cause or memory ceiling.

Explicit managed GPU Sandbox resources gpu/gpu_type; ephemeral class up to 8 GPUs with NVIDIA H100/H200/B300/RTX PRO 6000/RTX 4090/RTX 5090 and AMD MI355X documented. Shared fleet uses logical Earth placement and ignores requested geographic target; on-demand quota/capacity or immediate spot failure/preemption apply. Not inferred from agent hosting. Adapter requests no GPU and none was tested.

Tier 1/2 organization restrictions cannot be overridden by sandbox settings; Tier 3/4 default full egress and can set mutually exclusive CIDR/domain allowlists or block-all. Custom rules also restrict essential services. Runtime settings updates supported at higher tiers; upstream proxy is create-only. Adapter sets no policy; legacy HTTP block does not prove all egress is blocked.

Container disk survives stop/start/archive but memory does not; VM pause/resume retains memory and filesystem. Independent S3-backed Volumes and snapshots survive deletion. GPU sandboxes are deleted on stop and need external volumes for results. Adapter deletes sandbox at cleanup and does not test durable persistence.

Get existing sandbox, process sessions and persistent Python interpreter contexts supported. Current adapter creates a fresh sandbox on every execute and does not declare supports_session_calls; legacy agent_multiturn is one script, not distinct API calls. No pause/resume or cross-call reuse measured.

process.exec runs shell commands with cwd/env/timeout and supports persistent sessions/PTY via provider APIs. Adapter always uploads and runs a Python file, so shell-language requests are not implemented as a separate native route.

Provider byte upload/download, multiple-file and streaming APIs documented. Adapter uploads bytes but downloads only /tmp/transformed_output.txt, silently ignores failures and skips empty content. Legacy 6000-byte text result does not establish general binary, recursive or multi-file collection fidelity.

HTTP service preview URLs for ports 1-65535. Private standard preview token is sandbox-wide and unrevocable while running; signed URL token is single-port, expiring and revocable. Public sandbox property removes preview authentication. Adapter generates no preview and tests no ports.

Current BYOC supports customer-managed runners/custom regions with Daytona control plane and region Helm charts. Public daytonaio/daytona README states core development moved private in June 2026 and repository is unmaintained; legacy code remains usable/forkable as-is. Neither proves current managed GPU/VM feature parity in a fully self-operated deployment.

No managed Sandbox customer-KMS key binding/rotation/revocation contract verified in inspected sources. BYOC infrastructure control or independently encrypted object buckets is not a documented platform-wide CMEK guarantee. Adapter declares cmek_supported=False without testing key management.

pricing.model: Reserved vCPU/RAM/disk charges by lifecycle state, calculated per second; public base rates displayed hourly. GPU preemptible rates are a distinct schedule; on-demand amounts unavailable in retrieved page text.

rates.unit: GiB-hour after first 5 free (billed per second)
vCPU-hour; relationship to base compute not specified in retrieved pricing
GPU-hour (billed per second); pricing-only, not confirmed by inspected GPU type list
GPU-hour; amounts not available in retrieved official text
not explicitly priced in inspected sources

pricing.limitations: Public page retrieved 2026-10-13 carries publication metadata 2026-10-02; this is not a rate-change effective date. First-5-GiB allowance scope is not specified (do not assume per sandbox). Started and creating/starting/stopping/pausing reserve and bill resources; stopped/paused bill disk only, archived containers not billed, deleted sandbox not billed but retained snapshots can be. GPU free-credit exclusion is explicit in billing docs; advertised $200 free compute is not GPU entitlement. On-demand prices, GPU CPU/RAM additivity and independent volume tariff not verified. Pricing includes B200 but inspected sandbox supported-type list does not. Legacy fixed-rate report is not a metered invoice; no price-increase claim supported.
